name: Budapest Metropolitan University
summary: Budapest university with English-taught bachelor's degrees in art and design, business, communication and tourism, entered by online interview.

ib.text: No IB points rule: finish secondary school with overall marks above 50%. English is judged in a compulsory online interview (IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL 69 accepted, not required); art degrees need a portfolio.

programmes.name: Animation
programmes.about: Animation film from drawing to motion picture: design of characters and backgrounds, animation techniques, film tricks and games or apps; prior drawing or software experience helps but is not required.
programmes.overview: You follow a production from idea and script through storyboard and animatic to animation and post-production, studying story development, storyboard drawing, animation film language, drawing animation, puppet animation, 3D modelling and motion, 2D digital animation, sound design and compositing. Teaching is hands-on, with professional software and instructors from the industry. From the third semester you specialise in Creative Animation, which blends digital and classical techniques, or in 3D Animation, with spatial modelling and effects. Graduates work in animation studios, film production, game development, graphic design and advertising, or freelance.
programmes.ib: Portfolio of animation, drawing or other visual work, a motivation letter, CV and a statement that the work is your own.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio with motivation letter and CV, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Environmental Design
programmes.about: Design of spaces and objects with an ecological approach, taught through personal consultation and workshops where you build prototypes in the in-house workshop.
programmes.overview: The course explores how people relate to the built environment through interior and object design, sustainable and health-conscious solutions, CAD and 3D modelling, drawing, painting, form studies and design and art history. Year one introduces forms, spaces and materials through practical foundation work; year two focuses on interiors, furniture and architecture; year three centres on one large complex design project. Teaching relies on personal consultation, practical workshops with in-house prototyping and real-life internship placements. The specialisation is Interior and Spatial Design. Graduates work as interior designers, object designers, design consultants or independent artists.
programmes.ib: Portfolio with up to 20 drawings, up to 5 concept sketches or mock-ups and figure drawings, plus CV and motivation letter.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio with motivation letter and CV, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Film and Media Studies
programmes.about: Film history and theory with hands-on courses in directing, scriptwriting, cinematography, editing, sound and production management, in an international group.
programmes.overview: The first year covers film history, writing, directing, camera, lighting, editing and sound, with photography, documentary and short fiction projects. In year two you work on fiction scenes and feature films with actor direction, studio and multi-camera work, and short films from scripts developed in dramaturgy classes. Year three is concentrated practical work in writing, directing, editing, sound, music and producing, including preparing pitches for international platforms. Theory in film history, visual analysis and production management runs alongside. You find your role in directing, cinematography, editing, sound or producing, with internships at production companies, festivals and post-production firms.
programmes.ib: Portfolio, a short motivation letter about your background and why film and media, and a statement of ownership for the work.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio with motivation letter and CV, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Communication and Media Studies
separateFrom.reason: Film and Media Studies is an art degree in filmmaking (portfolio entry, EUR 3,990 a semester); Communication and Media Studies is a social-science degree entered by interview (EUR 3,200).

programmes.name: Graphic Design
programmes.about: Graphic design from illustration to book, identity and poster design, branding and packaging, moving to interactive and responsive work in the third year.
programmes.overview: The first year builds manual and digital skills through illustrations, covers, logos, pictograms and image identities. Year two covers book and magazine design, typography, packaging, branding, corporate identity and sustainable design, and year three turns to complex integrated projects, interactive and web graphics, mobile apps, UI and UX design and a diploma project. Teaching rests on individual consultations and project work on realistic briefs, supported by print workshops (screen printing, lithography, linocut, risography), laser cutters, 3D printers and bookbinding. You can specialise in Graphic Design or Packaging Design. Graduates work as freelance designers, art directors, illustrators and web or UI designers.
programmes.ib: Single PDF portfolio combining scanned handmade and digital work, plus a short motivation letter and a statement of ownership.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio with motivation letter and CV, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Media Design
programmes.about: Screen graphics, motion pictures, sound, 3D and game design, UX, visual effects and interactive installations, with the first year on visual logic and composition.
programmes.overview: The course trains media creators who shape technology with artistic sensitivity, across screen graphics, motion pictures, sound design, 3D, game design and UX design. Year one builds creative potential, visual logic and composition; year two deepens 2D and 3D design and interactive applications; year three is made up of complex projects carried out with industry professionals. You choose between two tracks: Multimedia, covering UX and web design, visual effects, sound design and projection mapping, or Game Design, covering visual, level and character design, storytelling and sound. Graduates work in post-production studios and game companies, or as independent media artists.
programmes.ib: Portfolio of drawings, images, sound, video or animation up to 5 minutes, interactive work or games that shows your professional competencies.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio with motivation letter and CV, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Communication and Media Studies
programmes.about: Communication theory, mass media, psychology and marketing, then a specialisation in International Communication or Integrated Media from the third semester.
programmes.overview: You study communication theory, advertising and media planning, digital marketing, and public relations theory and practice, together with social studies and psychology. Creative communication courses, social projects and media projects supply the practical side. From the third semester you choose International Communication, with cross-cultural skills, international relations and two working foreign languages, or Integrated Media, which teaches print, radio, television, online and social media together through project-based learning. Graduates work as journalists, editors, press officers and spokespeople, in PR and marketing management, event organisation and international affairs.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents and school results screened, then a compulsory online interview that also checks your English. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: International Relations
programmes.about: International, intercultural and transnational relations, with professional use of foreign languages, for careers in the international arena.
programmes.overview: The first semesters give broad introductions to the social sciences and the history of international relations, followed by core subjects such as diplomacy, international organisations, international law and modern international history, plus political science, economics, law and research methods. The course stresses communication, negotiation and writing. You choose between Diplomacy and International Communication, with security and foreign policy analysis and model diplomacy exercises, and International Development Cooperation, with a semester-long project. The final semester brings a thesis and a compulsory internship. Graduates become diplomats, policy analysts, NGO and think tank staff or public administrators, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Online interview with extra questions on current global issues. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Human Resource Management
programmes.about: HR processes and people: recruitment and selection, training, incentives and how technology is changing work (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The first three semesters give a business foundation, built on the idea that an HR specialist is a business expert focused on people, work processes and organisational culture. You then study the main HR functions: recruitment and selection, training and development, compensation, competency management, employer branding, labour law, industrial relations, organisational behaviour, leadership and performance management. Elective tracks are HR Branding, HR Technology and Digitalization, and HR Training and Development, and the final semester is practical experience in a company. Graduates work in multinationals, HR consultancies, recruitment and employer branding agencies, tech startups and the public sector.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents and school results screened, then a compulsory online interview. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: International Business Economics
programmes.about: EU integration and policies, world economic regions, foreign trade, international economics and finance and negotiation techniques (240 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The course covers EU integration and EU policies, globalisation and world economic regions, foreign trade strategy and international competitiveness, logistics, marketing fundamentals, management, international economics, international trade and finance, and negotiation techniques. It is designed to give knowledge that transfers across many positions in domestic and international business, and in civil and economic diplomacy. Graduates can work in business or in communication and social science fields, or continue to business programmes.
programmes.selectionNote: Documents and school results screened, then a compulsory online interview. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Business Administration and Management
programmes.about: Management and business knowledge with analytical and organisational skills for running business processes (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: You study accounting, business law, micro and macroeconomics, finance, human resources, management and organisation, marketing, statistics and strategic planning, with business informatics, controlling, logistics, project management and international economics. Teaching uses case studies of industry practice and a simulated business environment, and a partnership with the Young Entrepreneurs Association Hungary offers networking. You can add a specialisation in Financial Management, Global Marketing or International Business. Graduates become enterprise managers, business communicators, environmental managers, EU economic relations experts and start-up managers.
programmes.ib: Online Maths test as part of the admission interview; the test is set on your overall school results.
programmes.selectionNote: Online interview plus a 30-minute online Maths test, set by your overall school results. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Commerce and Marketing
programmes.about: Business and economics with commerce and marketing: brands, selling and group practical training (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: The first semesters cover the economic, social and technological environment and marketing fundamentals, followed by integrated marketing communications, market research, e-business, advertising and media planning, public relations, branding, digital and content marketing. Learning is project-based, with case studies and tasks set by leading companies under the guidance of industry experts. In the later semesters you specialise in Advertising and PR or Global Marketing, and the last semester combines a thesis and an internship. Graduates work as marketing experts in companies and agencies, start-up or SME managers and non-profit specialists.
programmes.ib: Online Maths test as part of the admission interview; the test is set on your overall school results.
programmes.selectionNote: Online interview plus a 30-minute online Maths test, set by your overall school results. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Finance and Accounting
programmes.about: Corporate finance, capital markets and financial processes, taught analytically with the latest financial tools and software (210 ECTS).
programmes.overview: You start with finance, corporate finance, accounting, calculus, statistics and business economics, then move to taxation, investments, financial law, strategic planning, audit, risk and control, insurance, project financing and management accounting. Specialised modules include accounting for financial institutions, controlling, accounting information systems, international financial accounting for multinationals, IT support for finance and consolidated annual reporting. Working with current software is emphasised, and you choose a Finance or an International Accounting specialisation. Graduates work in banking, securities, insurance, consulting and audit firms, corporate finance, tax advice and government finance.
programmes.ib: Online Maths test as part of the admission interview; the test is set on your overall school results.
programmes.selectionNote: Online interview plus a 30-minute online Maths test, set by your overall school results. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Tourism and Catering
programmes.about: Tourism and catering in Budapest, with third-year specialisations in Health Tourism or International Hotel Management (240 ECTS).
programmes.overview: Year one covers economics, marketing, statistics, law, tourism geography and leisure marketing. Year two introduces hotel management, catering and gastronomy, attractions and destination management and health tourism, and year three adds travel agency management, international negotiation, languages and a personal portfolio project. Teaching is project-based, with professional competitions, workshops, hotel visits, seminars at cooperating hotels. You specialise in Health Tourism (thermal baths, medical spas, wellness) or International Hotel Management, with work placements through partners such as Accor, Danubius and Mellow Mood. Graduates become hotel and spa managers, tour operators, tourism consultants and event organisers.
programmes.ib: Online Maths test as part of the admission interview; the test is set on your overall school results.
programmes.selectionNote: Online interview plus a 30-minute online Maths test, set by your overall school results. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: EU students pay the EU fee, which METU says includes EU and EEA member states and Turkey: EUR 2,800 to 3,990 a semester against EUR 3,500 to 4,990 for non-EU applicants; two semesters are paid up front.
The fee table for 2026/27 is indexed to Hungarian inflation, so it may rise each year; a EUR 150 application fee is non-refundable.
